# Mooncake

Mooncake is a declarative configuration management tool written in Go — "Docker for AI agents." It provides a safe, validated execution runtime with idempotency guarantees, dry-run support, and machine-readable output designed for AI agent consumption.

GitHub: https://github.com/alehatsman/mooncake
Schema: https://mooncake.dev/schemas/config.json

## Install

```sh
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alehatsman/mooncake/master/install.sh | sh
# or
go install github.com/alehatsman/mooncake@latest
```

## Basic Usage

```sh
# Run a playbook
mooncake run --config config.yml

# Dry run (safe preview — no changes applied)
mooncake run --config config.yml --dry-run

# Machine-readable output for AI agents (JSONL)
mooncake run --config config.yml --output agent

# Query system facts
mooncake facts
mooncake facts --format json
mooncake facts --query os --query arch

# Validate config without running
mooncake validate --config config.yml

# Generate a plan (without executing)
mooncake plan --config config.yml --format json
```

## Key Concepts

**Playbook** — A YAML file containing an ordered list of steps to execute.

**Step** — A single unit of work. Each step has a name and exactly one action. Steps support conditionals (`when`), loops (`with_items`, `with_dict`, `with_filetree`), tags, sudo, retry, and change/failure conditions.

**Preset** — A reusable, parameterized workflow (e.g., `preset: golang`, `preset: node`). Presets are expanded into steps at plan time. 330+ built-in presets ship with mooncake.

**Facts** — Auto-detected system information injected as template variables: `{{os}}`, `{{arch}}`, `{{cpu_cores}}`, `{{memory_total_mb}}`, `{{distribution}}`, `{{package_manager}}`, `{{home_dir}}`, `{{user}}`, `{{hostname}}`, and more.

**Idempotency** — Actions check current state before making changes. Re-running a playbook is safe; steps that are already in the desired state are skipped.

**Plan** — A serializable, pre-compiled execution plan. Generate with `mooncake plan`, execute with `mooncake run --from-plan plan.json`.

## Action Types

All actions are mutually exclusive within a step (use exactly one per step).

| Action | Category | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `shell` | command | Run a shell command string |
| `command` | command | Execute a binary directly (no shell, safer) |
| `file` | file | Create/delete files, directories, symlinks; set content, mode, owner |
| `template` | file | Render a Jinja2-style template to a destination file |
| `copy` | file | Copy a file with checksum verification |
| `download` | network | Download a file from a URL with checksum verification and retry |
| `unarchive` | file | Extract tar/tar.gz/zip archives with path traversal protection |
| `print` | output | Print a message to stdout |
| `vars` | data | Set variables in the execution context |
| `include_vars` | data | Load variables from an external YAML file |
| `preset` | system | Expand a named preset into steps |
| `service` | system | Manage services (systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS, Windows services) |
| `assert` | system | Verify system state — command exit codes, file existence/content, HTTP responses |
| `package` | system | Install/remove OS packages (apt, brew, dnf, pacman, etc.) |
| `wait` | system | Wait for a condition (port, file, HTTP, command) |

## Step Properties

```yaml
- name: Example step           # required
  shell: echo "hello"          # the action (one of the types above)
  when: "{{os}} == 'linux'"    # conditional — skip if false
  with_items: [a, b, c]        # loop over list; item available as {{item}}
  with_dict: {k: v}            # loop over dict; key/value as {{key}}/{{value}}
  tags: [setup, dev]           # for targeted execution (--tags flag)
  become: true                 # run with sudo
  changed_when: "false"        # override change detection
  failed_when: "false"         # override failure detection
  ignore_errors: true          # continue even if step fails
  register: result_var         # store result in variable
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    delay: 5
```

## Output Modes

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| (default) | Animated TUI with colored output for humans |
| `--output agent` | JSONL stream — one JSON object per event, for AI consumption |
| `--output json` | JSON-formatted console output |
| `--output quiet` | Suppress all output |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would change without applying anything |

### JSONL Event Schema (agent mode)

Each line is a JSON object with at minimum:
```json
{"event": "step.start", "step": "step-name", "timestamp": "..."}
{"event": "step.done", "step": "step-name", "changed": true, "duration_ms": 42}
{"event": "step.failed", "step": "step-name", "error": "...", "exit_code": 1}
{"event": "run.summary", "total": 5, "changed": 2, "skipped": 1, "failed": 0}
```

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | Success — all steps completed |
| 1 | Runtime failure — one or more steps failed |
| 2 | Validation error — config is invalid |
| 3 | Runtime error — unexpected internal error |

## JSON Schema

The schema for mooncake playbooks (YAML config files) is published at:

```
https://mooncake.dev/schemas/config.json
```

Use in VS Code (`settings.json`):
```json
{
  "yaml.schemas": {
    "https://mooncake.dev/schemas/config.json": ["*.mooncake.yml", "config.yml"]
  }
}
```

Generate locally:
```sh
mooncake schema generate --format json --output schema.json
```

## Template Variables

Templates use `{{variable}}` syntax (Jinja2-compatible). Built-in facts:

```
{{os}}               linux | darwin | windows
{{arch}}             amd64 | arm64 | armv7 | 386
{{distribution}}     ubuntu | debian | fedora | macos | ...
{{package_manager}}  apt | brew | dnf | pacman | ...
{{home_dir}}         /home/user or /Users/user
{{user}}             current username
{{hostname}}         system hostname
{{cpu_cores}}        integer
{{memory_total_mb}}  integer
{{kernel_version}}   string
```
